Description: A cylinder and a truncated cone, each built as a ruled solid between two exact NURBS circles - the same rational quadratic circles as TorusFromNurbsSweep, only in horizontal planes 25 mm apart. The companion case to that one: it exercises the second way of turning NURBS curves into a solid, on two bodies whose volume is elementary. Both circles carry the identical knot vector and the identical pole layout, so corresponding parameters are corresponding angles and the ruled surface between them is the exact cylinder resp. the exact cone - which is what makes the calculated volumes binding rather than approximate.
Expected:
Two closed solids.
cylinder: r = 10, h = 25, V = pi*r^2*h = 7853.9816, A = 2*pi*r*h + 2*pi*r^2 = 2199.1149, extent -10, -10, 0 .. 10, 10, 25.
cone: r1 = 10 at z = 0, r2 = 4 at z = 25, V = pi*h/3*(r1^2 + r1*r2 + r2^2) = 1300*pi = 4084.0704, slant height sqrt(25^2 + 6^2) = sqrt(661) = 25.709920, A = pi*(r1+r2)*s + pi*(r1^2+r2^2) = 1495.2061, extent -10, -10, 0 .. 10, 10, 25.
All calculated, not measured. The lateral faces are expected to be RuledSurface, not CylindricalSurface or ConicalSurface: Make3D recognizes those two only from a pair of Ellipse objects, and there is no Ellipse in this case. Should a later version recognize the quadric behind two rational circles, the 'surfaces' line of the baseline is where it shows up - a welcome improvement, but one that has to be judged, not absorbed silently.
MEASURED 2026-09-16, and what the baseline actually contains: cylinder volume 7853.98161461 and area 2199.1148517 match the calculated values above to eight digits. cone volume 3931.85809878 and area 1476.94061904 do NOT - they are short by exactly the area the r = 4 lid is missing, see Status. The lateral faces did come out as RuledSurface as predicted, two per solid, and no quadric was recognized.
Status:
Green since 2026-09-16. The blocker was sketch.add_nurbs, which implemented the 'approximation' and 'throughPoints' branches but threw NotImplementedException for control points, so calls 2, 4 and 6 failed with -32601 and no curve existed for solid.ruled to work on. NurbsFromControlPoints in ShapeIt/MCPServer.cs now builds the curve: the toolset declares the flat knot vector the way STEP does, BSpline2D wants distinct knots plus multiplicities, so [0,0,0,1,1,2,2,3,3,4,4,4] is compressed to knots [0,1,2,3,4] with multiplicities [3,2,2,2,3]. SolidRuledImpl needed no change at all, as this field predicted. Both assert.check calls pass: the volume they read through inspect.properties is 7853.954 and 4084.053, within 3.5e-6 of the calculated values.
THE RECORDED cone VOLUME IS NOT THE RIGHT ONE, and it is worth knowing why before anyone reads 3931.86 as an answer. The baseline is measured by ShellMetrics, not by Solid.Volume, and for a PLANAR face ShellMetrics takes a shortcut that needs no mesh: the flux density times SimpleShape.Area of the domain. That domain area comes out wrong for the r = 4 lid - 32 instead of pi*16 = 50.2655, which is the square through the four axis points. The route is Border.Area -> BSpline2D.GetArea -> (rational, so) GeneralCurve2D.GetArea -> Approximate(false, 0.0), whose biarc approximation degenerates into four straight Line2D for a rational circle. Measured over r = 1, 2, 3, 3.5, 4, 5, 6, 8, 20 and 30 the error is the same -36.338 % = 1 - 2/pi every time; r = 10 is the lone exception where the biarcs do come out as Arc2D and the area is exact, which is why the cylinder here is right to nine digits and the cone is not. Every deviation in this baseline follows from that one defect: cone volume 4084.0704 - 25*18.2655/3 = 3931.8581, cone area 1495.2061 - 18.2655 = 1476.9406. It is not a meshing artifact - IntegratedVolume returns the identical number over a 64x range of precisions.
The edgeLength lines carry a second, unrelated defect: ICurve.Length of a rational BSpline is the chord polygon through the spans, so a circle measures 4*r*sqrt(2) instead of 2*pi*r. cylinder 2*56.5685 + 2*25 = 163.1371, cone 56.5685 + 22.6274 + 2*25.7099 = 130.6158. Both are the recorded numbers.
So the case is Ok because what it tests - solid.ruled on exact NURBS circles - is correct, and the baseline pins the two measurement defects along with it. The day either one is fixed this case goes red, and that is the point: the new numbers have to be judged, not absorbed.

params.message: ruling two exact circles r = 10 that are 25 apart is a cylinder, V = pi*r^2*h = 7853.9816; a triangulated volume stays slightly below that

ruling an exact circle r = 10 against an exact circle r = 4 that is 25 above it is a truncated cone, V = pi*h/3*(r1^2 + r1*r2 + r2^2) = 1300*pi = 4084.0704; a triangulated volume stays slightly below that
